justifications.c1: The only enforcement figure is £5,445 fines and costs (Ward's Reservoir, search-confirmed) against a heritage owner for unfinished safety works, not missing records; Toddbrook's £12–56m is a rare non-farm catastrophe; compliance spend is tiny (NI £163.72/yr, £2,255 per 10-year inspection); no farm breach cost was found.
justifications.c2: The Act sets no default reading frequency (engineer-directed), the supervising engineer statement is annual, and incidents are rare (8 incidents in the 2023 report, no total failures 2023–24); weekly checks appear only as the EA's own fallback at Ward's.
justifications.c3: Manual prescribed-form record book (ICE) and directed visual inspections are documented, but there is no labour or cost figure for routine readings; engineer fees would not be removed by a sensor.
justifications.c4: Reservoirs Act 1975 s.11 requires a prescribed-form record of water levels, leakages and settlements and s.12 a supervising engineer (search-confirmed), with an EA offence-response ladder and prosecutions; but no enforcement against a farm undertaker and reform may partially deregulate ~55% of LRRs.
justifications.c5: Buyer is just 'the farm business' as undertaker with no job title or budget evidence; the market is tiny (~34 new farm LRRs in five years, search-confirmed via PQ HL16697) and compliance budgets are in the hundreds of pounds.
justifications.c6: Supervising engineers visit every registered reservoir yearly and direct reading intervals, but there is no evidence they sell, install or bundle monitoring.
justifications.c7: Dam-instrument vendors (Encardio, Senceive/Sisgeo) target large dams without published prices and ag level sensors do not produce compliance records; the gap is real but willingness to pay in this niche is not evidenced.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN level sensors exist but cost AUD 315–615 or €648 each, and seepage measurement needs a V-notch weir chamber at the toe drain (civil works, not self-install); BOM well above £50.
justifications.c9: The statutory record duty is perpetual while registered, but no comparable subscription pricing was found and reform may remove duties from many reservoirs.
justifications.c10: Regulator enforcement news (EA, non-farm) and farm trade press (FarmingUK, Strutt & Parker, NFU), but no first-hand farmer complaint about manual readings was found.

weakest: There is almost no money at stake for a farm undertaker: compliance costs are hundreds of pounds a year, the only fine found is £5,445 against a non-farm owner, and failures are extremely rare.
